instructions:
Which cloud: the user picks ONE cloud in the app (Settings → Which cloud): Vast (rented cards) or RunPod (serverless). video_studio_status shows it as cloud_provider. Only that cloud's tools and modes work; the other cloud's tools refuse with a message, so do not try to use them. If cloud_provider is "runpod" follow the RunPod paragraphs; if it is "vast" follow the Vast paragraph at the end (cards, gpu, vast_*), and ignore the RunPod ones. provider="cloud" or omitted means that cloud; provider="local" means the user's PC.
Model choice: list_workflows returns for each mode its license (open = free on the user's PC, paid = billed per result by a provider and needs an API key; RunPod modes are billed per second of GPU time), good_for (what it does best) and est_usd_per_result (typical USD price of one result). When the user describes a task, recommend the best-fitting mode (e.g. text inside images -> a paid GPT Image mode, quick cheap photoreal images -> Nano Banana, long free clips -> open-source), state the price in USD, and ask before using a paid one.
AI Video Studio For Windows generates AI video, pictures, voice and tools (open-source models such as Wan 2.2, LTX 2.5, FLUX, MiniMax H3) on a RunPod Serverless GPU endpoint (cloud, billed per second only while a job runs) or on the user's own PC, from the user's own desktop app. The app must be running on the user's PC.
RunPod: there are no cards to rent and no models to install; the models already live on the endpoint's network volume. RunPod is either "asleep" (max workers 0: nothing can run, so nothing can bill) or "awake". generate_video wakes it up by itself, and the app puts it back to sleep after the queue has been empty for a few minutes (auto_sleep_min, default 5). The first video after sleep takes 1-3 minutes longer. Use runpod_status to show the state and the estimated USD spent this session (session_usd), runpod_wake to wake it in advance, and runpod_sleep (e.g. when the user says they are done) so that nothing can bill. (Ελληνικά: runpod_status = αν κοιμάται/ξυπνά και πόσα ξοδεύτηκαν, runpod_wake = ξύπνα το, runpod_sleep = βάλ' το για ύπνο.)
Workflow:
1. Call video_studio_status first. If it fails, tell the user to open the "AI Video Studio For Windows" app.
2. Each result costs real money (about 0.02-0.25 USD on RunPod, see est_usd_per_result). Before generate_video, tell the user the model, length and rough cost in USD and get a clear yes. Only then pass user_confirmed=true. Batches: one confirmation for the whole batch is enough if the user approved the count and cost. generate_video returns est_usd (typical price of that result in USD) and runs_on (runpod, local or an API provider): repeat est_usd to the user.
3. generate_video returns a job id at once; generation takes 1-15 minutes (waking RunPod is the slow part). Poll with get_job (wait_seconds up to 45) until status is done or failed. Do not start duplicate jobs while waiting. For several videos send them all together.
4. When done, file_path is the .mp4 on the user's disk (est_cost_usd is the measured cost on RunPod). Pass it to editing tools/skills. Report failures with the error text; make_report gives a diagnostic file.
Prompts: write English, cinematic, concrete (subject, action, camera, lighting, style). For several clips of one story keep the same style words and character description in each prompt. For image-to-video give image_path (a local file) and describe only the motion.
The user may name a model ("LTX", "Wan") in plain words. Pass it as workflow_id exactly as the user said; the app resolves it (when RunPod is the default place to run it picks the RunPod mode of that model). To change the app's permanent defaults ("use LTX from now on", "run on my PC", "sleep after 10 minutes") call set_defaults. A per-video workflow_id/provider overrides the defaults for that video only.
Models: ltxv-t2v / ltxv-i2v are fastest and cheapest; wan22-* are higher quality and slower. For pictures set kind="image" (FLUX or SDXL). Modes named fal-* and replicate-* run on hosted APIs (pay per result, no GPU, need the provider key); the others run on RunPod (provider="runpod", the default) or on the user's PC (provider="local"). The app's default place to run is shown by video_studio_status. Use list_workflows to see the options and their parameters.
More than video: list_workflows also has voice (kind tts: text to speech; vc: change a voice), picture tools (kind i2i: remove background, upscale, edit with words), smoother motion (v2v) and lip-sync (lipsync). Each entry lists its "inputs" (image/audio/video slots) and, for voices, its "languages": answer language questions from that list, never from memory. Chain steps with generate_video: set workflow_id to the tool and give "inputs" like {"image":"job:<id of the finished job>"} or {"audio":"C:\\path\\voice.wav"}. Typical chains: picture -> video (i2v), text -> voice (tts) -> lip-sync (video with a face + that voice), video -> v2v. Every step costs or takes time like a video, so confirm the whole plan once. Tools that exist only as open-source modes without a RunPod twin run on the user's PC. For voice cloning, voice change and lip-sync on a real person, first make sure the user confirms the voice/face is their own or they have permission; do not help impersonate someone or make people appear to say things they did not say. For "make me a video with Wan 2.2 from this picture" use workflow_id "wan22-i2v-lightning" with image_path; from text only use "wan22-t2v-lightning". When the user says they are finished, ask and call runpod_sleep so that nothing can bill (the app also does it by itself after a few idle minutes). VAST (only when cloud_provider is "vast"): Cloud cards: generate_video rents a card by itself (the GPU the user named, e.g. 4090) and installs the model on it. The FIRST video after a card is rented takes about 15-20 minutes (boot + download of about 38 GB of Wan 2.2); tell the user this and the price per hour (list_gpus) before starting. While the card stays up (it closes itself after about 10 idle minutes) each next video takes only 2-4 minutes, so for several videos send them all together. When the user says they are finished, ask and call vast_stop with all=true so billing stops. For "make me a video with Wan 2.2 from this picture" use workflow_id "wan22-i2v-lightning" with image_path; from text only use "wan22-t2v-lightning". To have a card ready before the first video use card_start with workflow_id and gpu. Readiness: the card is ready only when vast_running shows ready=true (progress says what it is doing). Status "running" alone only means the machine started; the models still download for 10-25 minutes. After card_start, check vast_running every minute or two and TELL the user as soon as ready becomes true (and give the elapsed time and cost so far). Several cards at once: the app runs jobs in parallel on separate cards, up to card_max (default 2, settable 1-4 with set_defaults card_max). If the user wants two or more videos at the same time, send all the generate_video calls together (the app rents a second card by itself, each takes 15-20 minutes the first time) or call card_start with new_card=true to prepare an extra card in advance; tell the user each card is billed separately. Pictures only: for text-to-picture jobs (kind image, FLUX) the app uses its own cheap FLUX-only card that starts much faster than a video card; to prepare one call card_start with kind="image" (set_defaults image_card=false puts pictures on the video card instead). vast_running lists every card with its own ready, in_use and kind (video or images): send work only to ready cards, a card with ready=false is still downloading. The app checks all cards every minute and closes by itself a card that stopped, stopped answering for 3 minutes, never became ready in 45 minutes, or is idle for the auto-close time (set_defaults auto_close_min 5/10/30/0), and shows a notification; tell the user if vast_running shows fewer cards than before.

tools.name: video_studio_status
tools.description: Check that AI Video Studio For Windows is running and configured (API keys present, output folder, active jobs). Call this first.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List available generation modes/models (id, kind t2v|i2v|flf2v, VRAM, typical seconds, adjustable parameters with defaults and limits).

tools.name: runpod_status
tools.description: (Works only when RunPod is the cloud picked in the app; otherwise it refuses.) Show whether RunPod (the cloud GPU) is asleep, awake or working: state, workers_max (0 = asleep), jobs_waiting, session_usd (estimated USD spent by finished RunPod jobs since the app started), usd_per_hour_while_working and auto_sleep_min. Billing is per second only while a job runs; asleep means nothing can bill. Call it when the user asks what is running or what they are being charged. (Δείχνει αν το RunPod κοιμάται, είναι ξύπνιο ή δουλεύει και πόσα έχουν ξοδευτεί.)

tools.name: runpod_wake
tools.description: (Works only when RunPod is the cloud picked in the app; otherwise it refuses.) Wake RunPod up now (sets the endpoint's maximum workers to 1) so the next video starts sooner. Not needed before generate_video, which wakes RunPod by itself. Costs nothing until a job runs. (Ξυπνά το RunPod.)

tools.name: runpod_sleep
tools.description: (Works only when RunPod is the cloud picked in the app; otherwise it refuses.) Put RunPod to sleep (maximum workers 0): nothing can run or be billed. Call it when the user says they are finished. A job that is still running may fail, so check runpod_status / list_jobs first. (Βάζει το RunPod για ύπνο, σταματά κάθε χρέωση.)

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Queue ONE generation (costs real money). Ask the user for explicit confirmation including the approximate cost in USD first, then set user_confirmed=true. Returns a job id immediately plus est_usd (typical USD price of that result) and runs_on; RunPod is woken up automatically when it is asleep. Poll with get_job. Text-to-video by default; give image_path for image-to-video (and end_image_path for start->end frame).

user_confirmed.description: True only after the user explicitly agreed to the cost.

kind.description: image = still picture, audio = music, tts = speech, vc = voice change, i2i = picture tool, v2v = video tool, lipsync (default video).

provider.description: Where to run open-source modes: "local" = the user's PC, "cloud" = the cloud picked in the app (Vast or RunPod). Omit for the app default.

image_path.description: Local path of a start image (png/jpg) for image-to-video.

end_image_path.description: Local path of an end image (needs a flf2v workflow).

workflow_id.description: Model in the user's words ("ltx", "wan") or an id from list_workflows. Omit for the app's default.

scene.description: Scene number; the file gets a sNN_ prefix (keeps story order).

inputs.description: Media inputs by slot key (see the workflow's inputs): value "job:<job id>" = result of an earlier job, or a local file path (png/jpg/webp, mp3/wav/flac/ogg/m4a, mp4/webm/mov).

extra_params.description: Other workflow parameters by key (see list_workflows).

gpu.description: Vast only: GPU in the user's words ("4090", "RTX 3090 24GB"); omit for the app's default. Ignored on RunPod.

tools.name: set_defaults
tools.description: Change the app's defaults for all later videos (same as the settings in the app). model: free text like "ltx" or "wan". provider: "cloud" (default; the cloud picked in the app) or "local" (the user's PC). Vast only: gpu, card_max, image_card, auto_close_min (as before). auto_sleep_min: minutes with an empty queue before RunPod goes to sleep (0 = never). runpod_instance: the app can hold two separate RunPod instances (for example two accounts with their own billing); give 1, 2 or the instance name to switch which one runs everything. video_studio_status and runpod_status show the one in use (runpod_instance_name) and the configured ones (instances). Never switch instance unless the user asks.

provider.description: Default place to run open-source modes: cloud (the cloud picked in the app) or local (the PC).

runpod_instance.description: Which RunPod instance to use: 1, 2 or its name.

auto_sleep_min.description: Put RunPod to sleep after the queue has been empty for this many minutes (0 = never).

card_max.description: How many cards may run at the same time (1-4, default 2).

image_card.description: true (default) = pictures get their own cheap FLUX-only card; false = pictures use the video card.

auto_close_min.description: Close an idle card after 5, 10 or 30 minutes (0 = never).

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Status of a job. wait_seconds (max 45) waits until it finishes. status: queued|routing|generating|downloading|done|failed|cancelled. On done, file_path is the mp4.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: The 50 most recent jobs, newest first.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running job.

tools.name: retry_job
tools.description: Run a failed/cancelled job again (costs money again; ask first).

tools.name: make_report
tools.description: Write a diagnostic report file (settings without secrets, recent jobs, log tail) and return its path. Use when something fails repeatedly.

tools.name: list_gpus
tools.description: (Works only when Vast is the cloud picked in the app; otherwise it refuses.) Cloud GPUs currently offered with their USD per hour (min and median). Use it to estimate cost.

tools.name: card_start
tools.description: (Works only when Vast is the cloud picked in the app; otherwise it refuses.) Start a cloud card on Vast NOW and prepare it (the models download), without making a video yet. Costs money while it runs. Ask the user first, then set user_confirmed=true. Returns at once; poll vast_running until ready is true (status running alone is not enough), then call generate_video. You do not need it before generate_video (that starts a card itself), only to have the card ready in advance. Use new_card=true to add a second/third card for parallel work, and kind="image" for a picture-only card.

workflow_id.description: Mode whose models the card needs, e.g. wan22-i2v-lightning (default: the last used one).

gpu.description: GPU as the user said it, e.g. 4090 (default: the saved choice).

kind.description: image = cheap picture-only card (FLUX), video = card with Wan (default).

new_card.description: true = rent one MORE card even if a card is already up or starting (two or more cards in parallel, up to card_max).

tools.name: vast_running
tools.description: (Works only when Vast is the cloud picked in the app; otherwise it refuses.) List the cloud cards currently rented on Vast (GPU, status, minutes running, cost so far, USD per hour). Every card listed is billed while it exists, even while loading. Call it when the user asks what is running or what they are being charged. Also returns ready (true only when ComfyUI on the card can accept work) and progress (text while it is not ready). Each card has its own ready, in_use and kind (video/images); also card_max.

tools.name: vast_stop
tools.description: (Works only when Vast is the cloud picked in the app; otherwise it refuses.) Close (destroy) a rented Vast card so billing stops: give id from vast_running, or all=true to close all of the app's cards. A job running on it will fail. Ask the user first, then set user_confirmed=true.

all.description: Close all of the app's cards (use instead of id).
